segments.translation: It really didn’t. That is what I was thanking God for at night. For watching us in Jay.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: The wind was blowing hard.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: If we really think about it. It has been missing us.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: Exactly.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That tornado will go on that side, or on this side. And where we come from—it will be good.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: That is what has been happening all this time, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: But we have been told, “I will never forsake you.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: No, He really didn’t.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: There was a tree that fell in my neighbor’s yard, and my yard was clear. I praise God for that, but I felt sorry for him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: But it didn’t harm him.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: It really didn’t. Yes, God is good. That is why we are here. That is our testimony.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I was talking, too... who was that preacher? I was talking, to. He said, “Now is the time. It is too... for preaching. We are getting close.”

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: It’s true—preaching and teaching both, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: The way we live, and the way we talk, is what they need. To see who we depend on.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: That we are different.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And it also says to love one another.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: Exactly, that it true. Love seems to be running out, nowadays.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: Charlie Shell’s dad, was Waleli, would say that. He would say, “Let’s [unintelligible] again. Let’s sing the song that says we love one another.”

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: I have heard that, too. I was thinking about it the other day. A while back. You know the elderly men, not old men, just young men like Herbert Turner—they really did like going to church. Sunday morning, Wednesday night, and Sunday they were ready to go to church. Today you don’t see young people in church.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: The world has too much to offer, and they prefer that more.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Where I was pastoring, playing ball was pulling them away.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: It is the same everywhere.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: That is true.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: One time I told them this, I don’t know if they got upset with me. I said, “If things start happening to y’all, or if y’all get sick. Pray to playing ball and see what it does for you.”

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: That is when they will look for a preacher, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: Or they will say, “That-One really should not have said that.”

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: I am not going back again, to that preaching.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It was funny what one said. He said, “Why is it that when you go to McDonald’s, and, if they don’t get your order right, y’all get mad. And then, the next morning y’all go that way again [to McDonald’s]. And, if it’s at church, y’all see one thing wrong—y’all stop going.”

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: They will quickly mistake things, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: “And if it’s McDonald’s, y’all will go every morning,” he said.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: Y’all will be getting cheated.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: It really is like that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: This Cherokee that we speaking, or that we did speak. What do you think is going to happen to it? As time goes on, is it going to fade away? Is it going to keep going for several more years in time?

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: It is going to fade away if they do not make an effort to learn it. You really have to make an effort to learn. Because, like we were saying, they are talking different. They don’t talk how we talk. It is going to end when us-that-are-elders leave, pass away, the young people will not know anything.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: It is going to be hard for them nowadays, if they don’t pay attention to what is right. To go in the right way. It is going to be hard for them because the devil --

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: -- is going to deceive them.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: He will be worse than he is today.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What about this Cherokee that they are learning. How they are taught, it sounds a little different, ain’t it?
Yes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Do y’all think it will continue like that, in several more years in time, how they are taught?

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: How they are being taught is how it will be. Those little ones that are learning—when they get to their house and, if parents don’t know how to speak, it means nothing.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: If the parents don’t speak Cherokee, ain’t it, yeah.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: That is just the way it is going to be.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It would be joyful if they will hold on tight.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: Yes, it would be joyful.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They might do that.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: If they hold on to what is right, it would really be good.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: And, also if someone teaches them that speaks good Cherokee, like we are talking. If someone like that teaches them, they will learn a lot.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Some sounds different, on how they are teaching.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: Even if you say the tone different, it means something different.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: A while ago they called me over there. And they said, “How do you say this?” The way they talk sounded different, and it was also different to understand.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: That is true. And some that are Cherokee are bashful to speak Cherokee. It makes me mad when someone does that. I tell them, “You are just Cherokee, so speak Cherokee.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: If you talk to them, they say, “I don’t understand.” And their parents can really speak Cherokee.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: Yeah, they barely learned English. I don’t like that.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: Us elders can’t teach.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: I teach my grandkids Cherokee. Some will speak, and some will just run away.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: They don’t want to listen.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: No.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Our grandkids, at the house, my wife teaches them. Then, when they go down the hill, they are taught there again. They are learning pretty good now.
That is good.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: It is good to speak Cherokee. I am thankful.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Me too.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: That I can speak Cherokee.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: That was what they were saying—that is part of our culture. The main part is the language.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It is important.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: It is important.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Sometimes White people come to the church when we sing in all Cherokee. They say, “It sounds extremely beautiful, don’t ever lose it.” But it is going to be good if we don’t lose it.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: That’s true.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: Even when we sing, we don’t have to have instruments, ain’t it? You can sing good in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: It is beautiful without instruments.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You singing Cherokee is the best sound out of other tribes, some say.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: I believe that, too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What do you think about this conversation? Does it seem good that Cherokee Nation has prepared this for us to talk?

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: If it is helpful to someone, it is good. If they can learn, like what we are talking about.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: If the little ones can learn, I would think it would be joyful.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So y’all think it is good that we are doing this because of Cherokee Nation?

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: It is good.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: Y’all work really hard.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, they work really hard. The real plan is they do not want to lose the Cherokee language. And also, if the students hear it, they might learn a little something. That is their plan here.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: And the chief, what is his name in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What is his name, this chief that we have?

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: Dudovni.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: But anyway, he is going to be on tomorrow at nine o’clock on channel six.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Tomorrow morning.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: I am going to watch him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Is he doing pretty good?

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: At nine o’clock.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: At nine, channel six.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: He is attacked. When people attack one another... what does it say in the Bible? They may be doing something little, but when we look at it, it could be bigger. We might be doing something worse.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: It says, “Wipe the mote from your own eye.”

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: It really is like that, that is right.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: That is what the natives are like, and also jealousy is involved.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That is what is taking over.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: If someone is doing good, they will still find something to blame them for.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: That is sad, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: If something good happens to somebody, I am thankful. Praise the Lord.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: That is how we are supposed to be. There is no reason to get mad. They done it theirself, they bought it on theirself.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s it. They learned it theirself. I don’t know anything, even if someone is saying something.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Me too, we... I appreciate it, I appreciate us having this conversation.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: We didn’t know what you were going to ask us.

segments.speaker: wallora-kingfisher
segments.translation: We didn’t, did we?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: We are from Jay. We could have just talked over there.

segments.speaker: oleta-pritchett
segments.translation: That is true. Wali would not have gotten lost.
